title: Built-in Validation for Minimal APIs with AddValidation()
description: Use the new AddValidation() method in .NET 10 to automatically validate Minimal API parameters and return structured validation errors.

data.text: Before .NET 10, validating input in Minimal APIs required manually checking each parameter, writing custom validation endpoints, or pulling in FluentValidation with additional boilerplate. There was no built-in, convention-based validation pipeline like the one available in controller-based APIs with Data Annotations.

.NET 10 introduces the AddValidation() method on the Minimal API builder. This method scans your endpoint parameters for validation attributes and automatically enforces them. When validation fails, a standardized ProblemDetails response is returned without any additional code.

data.title: Configure AddValidation in Program.cs
data.content: Enable built-in validation for Minimal API parameters

data.text: When validation fails, AddValidation() returns a 400 Bad Request with a ProblemDetails body that includes all validation errors grouped by property name. This matches the behavior of controller-based APIs, providing a consistent developer experience across both paradigms.

data.title: Sample validation error response
data.content: The ProblemDetails response when a request fails built-in validation

data.text: If you already use FluentValidation, AddValidation() integrates seamlessly. Register your FluentValidation validators as usual, and the built-in pipeline will automatically invoke them alongside Data Annotation validators.

data.title: Using FluentValidation alongside AddValidation
data.content: Register a FluentValidation validator and let AddValidation invoke it automatically

data.title: Key Benefits
items: Works with Data Annotations and FluentValidation simultaneously.

data.title: Summary
points: Call AddValidation() in the service container to enable built-in validation.
Apply [Validate] to endpoint parameters to opt in.
Use Data Annotations or FluentValidation — both are supported.
Validation errors are returned as ProblemDetails with a 400 status code.
data.takeaway: AddValidation() brings controller-style validation to Minimal APIs with zero custom middleware, making .NET 10 Minimal APIs production-ready for complex input validation scenarios.
